teaser.en: The stems of this grass help make the *kayamba*, the shaken rattle that keeps rhythm at coastal dances.

summary.en: *Mchuchi* is the name for the tall thatching grasses of grassland and fallow. It thatches roofs and supplies stems for the *kayamba* rattle.

about.en:
*Mchuchi* is a group of tall, tufted grasses that grow in dense clumps. Their flowering heads are distinctive: the spikelets come in pairs, each pair wrapped in a leaf-like sheath, giving the top of the stem a ragged, layered look.

As they dry, the grasses turn a warm reddish brown, which is where the English name 'red grass' comes from.

where.en: Look for *mchuchi* in grassland and on fallow land. It is easiest to recognise late in the season, when the stands turn red-brown.

uses.en:
*Mchuchi* is cut for thatch, the long, tough stems laid in layers on roofs.

Its stems are also used to make the *kayamba*, the flat rattle of reed stems filled with seeds that is shaken to keep rhythm in coastal music.

names.en: Digo: *mchuchi*, also *mdembe*. Note that *mdembe* is also the name of a different thatching grass (*Hyperthelia dissoluta*). English: thatching grass or red grass. No Swahili name has been recorded. Scientists place it in the genus *Hyparrhenia*.

reason.en: Another thatching grass, sharing the name mdembe
Tall grass of the same grassland and fallow
Doum palm, another thatching and craft plant
Coconut palm, the main source of makuti thatch

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
